The word “courses” was being misunderstood. The student was attending a cafeteria meal consisting of a prearranged sequence of dishes, not looking at university classes. Each course was served in turn, and when the next course arrived, cafeteria staff cleared the preceding dishes—some partly eaten and some uneaten. Thus, over the evening, every course disappeared from the table before the student could choose among them, while the student still had to choose university courses before the registration deadline.
